title: Illusion of Gaia
subtitle: Quintet · Super Nintendo Entertainment System

body: Illusion of Gaia is Quintet's Super Nintendo action role-playing adventure about Will, a boy drawn into a journey through a fantasy version of Earth. Ancient ruins and monuments provide its destinations, including places inspired by the Great Wall and the pyramids. Will travels with friends whose relationships give the expedition a personal story alongside its larger danger. The adventure connects discovering old places with learning about the young people crossing them, allowing a distant landmark to become the setting for a small, immediate human problem.

Will can transform through Dark Space into Freedan and, later, Shadow. Each form offers different strengths and abilities, giving obstacles more than one possible relationship to the controlled character. Freedan's sword provides greater reach in combat, while Will's techniques are especially useful for finding routes through the environment. The player learns to recognise where a change is needed. A passage seen earlier can become accessible after another ability has been learned, connecting the character's development to the shape of the ruins being explored.

Clearing a room of enemies grants a permanent improvement to attack, defence or health, tying development to completing an area rather than repeatedly gathering experience. The journey advances through a sequence of places with limited opportunities to return, making attention to optional Red Jewels useful along the way. Mariko Ōhara contributed the story and Moto Hagio the artwork. Released in Europe as Illusion of Time, the game gives its growing cast and transformations a shared setting in the remnants of civilisations whose stories are still affecting the present.
story_headings: A boy follows the traces of an older world
